title: Chapter 8 Mastery Quiz: Contemporary Trends, Diversity & the Replication Crisis
description: Demonstrate comprehensive mastery of WEIRD sampling, evolutionary genetics, open science reforms, and computational neuroscience.

questions.question: What proportion of participants in top psychological journals came from Western nations in Henrich et al.'s 2010 survey?

options.text: Roughly 96% of participants (from nations representing only 12% of the globe)
Exactly 50%
Less than 10%
100% of participants were from Antarctica

questions.explanation: Henrich et al. showed that 96% of subjects were drawn from WEIRD nations representing only 12% of the global population.

questions.question: Why did San hunter-gatherers of the Kalahari Desert not fall prey to the Müller-Lyer optical illusion?

options.text: They grew up in a non-carpentered visual environment lacking urban right-angle architectural corners
They had superhuman genetic visual acuity
They were blind in one eye
They refused to look at the test paper

questions.explanation: The 'carpentered world' hypothesis explains that individuals in non-carpentered environments do not interpret acute/obtuse angles as depth markers.

questions.question: In cross-cultural cognition, how does East Asian cognitive style generally compare to Western cognitive style?

options.text: East Asian cognition tends to be more holistic and relationship-centered; Western cognition tends to be more analytic and object-centered
East Asians have no working memory
Westerners cannot perceive colors
Both cognitive styles are 100% identical in every culture

questions.explanation: Richard Nisbett's work demonstrated holistic, relational processing in East Asian populations versus analytic, categorized processing in Western populations.

questions.question: What is the primary premise of modern Evolutionary Psychology?

options.text: Human psychological mechanisms are specialized cognitive adaptations shaped by natural selection in ancestral environments
All human behaviors are learned from television
Animals evolved from computers
Humans will stop evolving within 10 years

questions.explanation: Evolutionary psychology analyzes human cognitive mechanisms as functional adaptations to ancestral survival and reproductive challenges.

questions.question: What does heritability (h^2) measure in behavioral genetics?

options.text: The proportion of observable variance in a trait within a population attributable to genetic variation
The exact percentage of an individual person's trait caused by their parents' genes
The speed of neural transmission across generations
The likelihood that a mutation will cause immediate death

questions.explanation: Heritability estimates the proportion of phenotypic variation within a specific population that is accounted for by genetic variance.

questions.question: How does epigenetics challenge rigid genetic determinism?

options.text: It demonstrates that environmental experiences turn genes on or off via molecular chemical tags without altering the underlying DNA sequence
It proves that genes do not exist
It shows that DNA can be rewritten by conscious willpower alone
It proves that all twin studies were fraudulent

questions.explanation: Epigenetics demonstrates that environmental factors regulate gene activation (methylation/acetylation) dynamically throughout life.

questions.question: What shocking event occurred in 2011 that catalyzed psychology's Replication Crisis?

options.text: A top APA journal published a paper claiming statistically significant evidence for psychic precognition (ESP)
All psychology departments were shut down by federal law
Computers achieved general artificial superintelligence
Sigmund Freud's personal diary proved he was an actor

questions.explanation: Daryl Bem's 2011 JPSP paper reporting statistically significant precognition exposed deep flaws in standard statistical testing practices.

questions.question: What is 'p-hacking' (or researcher degrees of freedom)?

options.text: Manipulating data collection, removing outliers, and testing multiple variables until finding a statistically significant p < .05 result
Hacking into another researcher's password-protected laptop
Writing peer-reviewed papers using artificial intelligence
Refusing to collect survey responses

questions.explanation: P-hacking involves opportunistically tweaking statistical choices until non-significant noise appears statistically significant.

questions.question: What is 'HARKing' in scientific research?

options.text: Hypothesizing After the Results are Known
Hearing Auditory Reflexes in Kittens
Having All Researchers Know
Hiding Academic Rejection Letters

questions.explanation: HARKing involves presenting post-hoc unexpected findings as if they were confirmatory predictions formulated prior to testing.

questions.question: What is the 'File Drawer Problem' (publication bias)?

options.text: Academic journals primarily publish positive significant results, while null replication failures remain hidden away in file drawers
Filing cabinets are a fire hazard in universities
Researchers lose their questionnaires in office desks
Digital cloud storage makes physical paper files obsolete

questions.explanation: Publication bias leads to a distorted scientific literature where 20 failed replications are hidden while 1 false-positive lucky study is published.

questions.question: In the 2015 Open Science Collaboration Reproducibility Project led by Brian Nosek, what percentage of landmark psychology studies successfully replicated?

options.text: Approximately 36% to 39%
Exactly 0%

questions.explanation: Only about 36% to 39% of 100 examined psychological findings replicated their original significant findings.

questions.question: What Open Science practice requires researchers to register their hypotheses, sample size, and analysis plans publicly before collecting data?

options.text: Preregistration
Introspection
Retraction
Extinction

questions.explanation: Preregistration locks down research plans beforehand, preventing post-hoc p-hacking and HARKing.

questions.question: What is a 'Registered Report' in scientific publishing?

options.text: A format where peer review and publication acceptance occur before data collection, regardless of whether results turn out positive or null
A paper that has been patented for corporate profit
A police investigation of academic misconduct
A government-censored medical study

questions.explanation: Registered Reports evaluate the methodology and theory prior to testing, eliminating publication bias against null results.

questions.question: Which of the following famous psychological claims failed to replicate under rigorous multisite open-science replication?

options.text: Social elderly priming (walking slower after unscrambling words about the elderly)
Classical conditioning of salivation in dogs
The existence of visual photoreceptor rods and cones
Nerve conduction taking physical time

questions.explanation: John Bargh's elderly priming effect was among several high-profile social psychology findings that failed robust replication.

questions.question: What is the Human Connectome Project seeking to construct?

options.text: A comprehensive network wiring diagram of all anatomical and functional pathways in the human brain
A complete list of every book ever written about psychology
A worldwide database of Facebook friendships
An artificial clone of Sigmund Freud

questions.explanation: The Human Connectome Project maps the complex structural and functional network topology of the living brain.

questions.question: What is 'Digital Phenotyping' in modern behavioral science?

options.text: Continuous, real-time quantification of individual human behavior and mental states using sensors from smartphones and wearables
Creating video game avatars that look like celebrities
Taking photos of patients' teeth
Printing 3D plastic brains

questions.explanation: Digital phenotyping captures moment-by-moment behavioral data passively from consumer digital devices.

questions.question: How do modern deep learning convolutional neural networks compare with the human visual ventral stream?

options.text: They exhibit striking functional similarities in hierarchical feature extraction from edges to complex object shapes
They have absolutely zero mathematical similarity to biological vision
They are identical in every chemical detail including blood flow
They were proven to be psychic by Daryl Bem

questions.explanation: Deep neural networks extract visual features in hierarchical tiers that closely model processing in mammalian visual cortex (V1 to IT cortex).

questions.question: What is the historical cycle observed in the evolution of psychology from antiquity to the present?

options.text: From philosophical contemplation of mind to biological laboratory science, to behavioral reduction, back to computational cognition and integrative neuroscience
From complete knowledge in ancient Greece to total ignorance today
From studying only animals to studying only plants
From computer programming back to stone-age superstition

questions.explanation: Psychology evolved from philosophy of mind to laboratory science, narrowed to behavior, and re-expanded into cognitive and integrative neuroscience.

questions.question: What movement within modern clinical psychology emphasizes relying strictly on treatments validated by randomized controlled trials (RCTs)?

options.text: Evidence-Based Practice (Empirically Supported Treatments)
Orthodox Freudian Psychoanalysis
Mesmeric Animal Magnetism
Phrenological Cranioscopy

questions.explanation: Evidence-Based Practice mandates that clinical therapies demonstrate empirical efficacy in peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials.

questions.question: What did the Open Science movement reveal about the importance of scientific self-correction?

options.text: A scientific discipline gains strength not by pretending to be infallible, but by transparently uncovering errors and reforming its methods
Psychology should be eliminated from universities
Scientists should never share their data with others
All scientific papers before 2015 should be burned

questions.explanation: The replication crisis proved that science is defined by transparent institutional self-correction and reproducibility.

questions.question: Which field of psychology investigates how neurological processes, genetic factors, and socio-cultural environments dynamically interact to produce mental health?

options.text: The Biopsychosocial Model
Classical Structuralism
Cartesian Substance Dualism
Radical Behaviorism

questions.explanation: George Engel's biopsychosocial model integrates biological, psychological, and social factors into a unified holistic framework.

questions.question: What core philosophical quest connects Wilhelm Wundt's 1879 Leipzig lab with 21st-century artificial intelligence and neuroscience?

options.text: The fundamental endeavor to explain how conscious subjective experience and purposeful behavior emerge from physical systems
The goal of proving that animals do not feel pain
The attempt to replace human workers with steam machines
The commercial advertising of sugar products

questions.explanation: From Wundt to modern computational neuroscience, psychology's enduring quest is solving how subjective mind and behavior emerge from physical architecture.
